Class DraftApplicationService

java.lang.Object
edu.ucsb.cs.taapply.services.DraftApplicationService
@Service public class DraftApplicationService extends Object
The writes that keep a student from having both a draft and a finalized application to the same recruitment (issue #417). A finalized application is one that is not CANCELLED: one who cancelled may start again (issue #318), with a new draft, or turn the cancelled application back into a draft (issue #420).

Each method is one database transaction. Submitting saves the application and deletes the draft (and the admin's comments on it) together, so a failure part way leaves neither the new application nor a missing draft behind. Opening or saving a draft checks, in the same transaction as the write, that the student has no application yet. Turning a cancelled application back into a draft creates the draft and deletes the application together.

The rule cannot be a database constraint: it spans two tables, and the only way to enforce it in the database would be a trigger written twice, once for H2 and once for Postgres. The admin's Applications and Draft Applications pages report any student who breaks it.

    • requireNoApplication

      public void requireNoApplication(String email, Long recruitmentId)

    • submit

      @Transactional public void submit(Application application)
      Saves a newly submitted application and deletes the draft it grew from, in one transaction. Whatever an admin wrote about the draft carries over to the application (issue #296), and is deleted with the draft; if any of these writes fails, none of them is kept.

    • open

      @Transactional public DraftApplication open(String email, Long recruitmentId)
      The student's draft for the recruitment, created empty if there is none; refused if they already have an application to it. If the same person's form opened twice at once, the second insert breaks the unique constraint and the exception is thrown out of this transaction for the caller to answer with the draft the first one made.

    • save

      @Transactional public DraftApplication save(DraftApplication draft)
      Saves a draft; refused if the student already has an application to its recruitment.

    • resumeCancelled

      @Transactional public DraftApplication resumeCancelled(String email, Long applicationId)
      Turns one of the student's cancelled applications back into a draft (issue #420): "Create a new application". In one transaction it creates the draft from the application's answers, moves the admin's comments on the application to the draft (they go back to the application on submit, issue #296), deletes the faculty's rankings of the application and deletes the application. If any of these fails, none is kept: the cancelled application stays and there is no draft.

      Refused with 404 for an unknown application, 403 for someone else's, and 400 unless the application is cancelled, its recruitment is accepting applications, and the student has neither a live application nor a draft for it. Only this application is deleted: an older cancelled one to the same recruitment stays, and the next submission's attempt number is one more than the highest left.

      The audit trail of an admin's edits to the application is kept: it is history, and it has no foreign key to the application, so its rows simply name an id that no longer exists. If the same person asks twice at once, the second draft insert breaks the unique constraint and the exception is thrown out of this transaction, as for open(String, Long).
